content.text:
Confirmed: `init()` creates the `TickCounter` but never calls `reset()` on it, so with the constructor setting `tickCount = maxTicks`, the very first `update()` call would immediately return `true` (round over) before any ticks ever ran — a clear bug introduced when `TickCounter` was created in commit 78b1499.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 78b1499979980454269b65e83e8561a22c45b95f

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit `ea146d3` touches many files, but most of that is an unrelated feature refactor (replacing `RoundEndData`/`NextRoundEvent` with `ServerReadyEvent`/`AllPlayersReadyEvent`). The one change that is a pure, self-contained bug fix is in `core/src/de/gg/util/TickCounter.java`, where the constructor line `tickCount = maxTicks;` is removed, along with the javadoc note "Has to be reset first to get used." I ran `git log --follow` on `TickCounter.java` and found it only has two revisions: it was created in `78b1499` and then fixed in `ea146d3`. There is no earlier history for this file, so the bug must have been introduced at its creation.

**(2) The specific defect:** In `78b1499`, `TickCounter`'s constructor initialized `tickCount = maxTicks` (i.e., the counter starts already "full"). `GameSession.init()` (also introduced in the same commit) constructs the `TickCounter` and never calls `reset()` before gameplay starts. Since `TickCounter.update()` checks `if (tickCount == maxTicks)` and returns `true` once when `finished` is false, the very first call to `update()` after initialization would immediately report "round over" — before a single real tick/round had been processed. This is a classic off-by-initialization bug: the round-end condition is satisfied at construction time instead of after `TICKS_PER_ROUND` actual ticks occur.

**(3) Supporting evidence:**
- `git show 78b1499 -- core/src/de/gg/util/TickCounter.java` shows the class being newly added with `tickCount = maxTicks;` in the constructor.
- `git show 78b1499:core/src/de/gg/game/GameSession.java` shows `init()` instantiating the `TickCounter` and never calling `reset()`, and `update()` directly delegating to `tickCounter.update()`.
- The fix commit `ea146d3` removes exactly that line and removes the javadoc instructing callers to `reset()` first, which is the minimal change needed to eliminate the premature "round over" signal.

I'm fairly confident in this attribution since the buggy field and the fixing diff line up exactly within a single, newly-created file, and no other commit touches `TickCounter.java` in between.
